author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A Kenyan court has convicted religious leader Paul Mackenzie and 29 followers over the deaths of 191 children in the Shakahola forest case, one of the country’s most devastating criminal investigations.

Judge Diana Kavedza-Mochache ruled that prosecutors had proved their case against Mackenzie and his associates. The court heard that children were allegedly coerced into starving themselves in the belief that they would meet Jesus. Evidence also described children being tied to trees, beaten and strangled.

The wider Shakahola investigation has linked the deaths of more than 400 people to the religious group’s activities. Many victims remain missing or unidentified, and investigations into the deaths are continuing.

Steven Mwiti, who lost six children, described the devastating impact of the tragedy on his family. Defence lawyer Lawrence Obonyo criticised the court’s reasoning and the introduction of crimes against humanity charges, signalling that the defence intends to appeal.

title: Kenya court convicts Paul Mackenzie over deaths of 191 children

description:
France is assessing the damage from a weekend of violent unrest, with more than 3,000 businesses affected by looting, vandalism and arson in Paris and other cities. The French Chamber of Commerce estimates losses running into hundreds of millions of dollars, while Interior Minister Laurent Nunez has acknowledged that police lost control during parts of the protests. More than 500,000 people demonstrated peacefully across France on Saturday, demanding better conditions for students and action on the rising cost of living, before violence erupted in several urban centres. The government has promised a major criminal justice response, including targeted curfews, while President Emmanuel Macron has proposed giving local authorities greater powers to ban demonstrations. Protests continued on Monday, with students forcing the Louvre Museum to close over cuts to cultural funding. Further nationwide demonstrations are planned for Saturday, led by the Yellow Vests movement.

description:
The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) says funding shortages have forced it to cut food assistance to around 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza, raising fears of worsening hunger as winter approaches. The agency says it is halving food rations, reducing cash assistance and providing fewer cooked meals, despite the continued need for humanitarian support. WFP Acting Executive Director Carl Skau says a massive aid operation has helped push back famine since the ceasefire began, but warns that the progress remains fragile. He stresses that the reductions are driven by a lack of funding, not declining needs or difficulties bringing food into Gaza. For displaced families who have lost their homes and livelihoods, humanitarian aid remains a vital source of food. Community kitchens are also under increasing pressure as families struggle to afford even basic meals. 

Al Jazeera's Hind Khoudary reports from Gaza.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Former Israeli Defence Minister Benny Gantz has announced his withdrawal from the October 27 election, just over a week before voters head to the polls. Gantz, who leads the Blue and White party, said his decision was aimed at preventing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his right-wing coalition from securing another term. Recent opinion polls suggested his party could fail to cross the electoral threshold needed to enter parliament, potentially wasting votes that might otherwise benefit the opposition. His withdrawal could reshape the race as opposition parties, including those led by Gadi Eisenkot and Avigdor Lieberman, face pressure to overcome their differences and consolidate support. Netanyahu's coalition partners are also urging smaller right-wing parties to withdraw to avoid splitting their vote. With neither political camp appearing assured of enough seats to form a government, coalition negotiations may still be necessary after the election. 

Al Jazeera's Nour Odeh repo
title: Benny Gantz withdraws from Israel's election race in bid to unseat Netanyahu

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Violent clashes between protesters and riot police have erupted in Paris as unrest spreads across France, leaving businesses and public buildings damaged in several cities.

Al Jazeera's Natacha Butler reports from Place de la République, where demonstrations over the cost of living escalated into scuffles and police used tear gas. Residents describe fear and uncertainty, while business owner Alberto Carvalho calls the aftermath “hell”.

In Limoges, City Hall was set on fire. Mayor Guillaume Guerin criticised the lack of resources available to protect the building as the city dealt with the destruction.

French President Emmanuel Macron has addressed the nation, expressing support for affected shopkeepers and promising that the government will not leave business owners to face the consequences alone.

As cleanup efforts begin in Rennes following overnight violence, questions remain over how the government will address public grievances, support affected communities and restore calm.
title: France unrest: Macron vows support for businesses hit by violence

description:
US President Donald Trump has publicly endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel’s scheduled October 2026 elections, highlighting their partnership and shared campaign against Iran.

Netanyahu has pointed to what he describes as their success in “crushing” the Iranian axis as a reason to continue working together. But analysts Patty Culhane, Negar Mortazavi and Alan Eyre examine the complexities of the alliance, including the conflict’s unpopularity among parts of the US public and Trump’s emphasis on personal relationships and political legacy in foreign policy.

The report also looks at tensions within Israel, where protesters in Tel Aviv have demonstrated against National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir as his party reportedly gains ground in opinion polls.

With the election approaching, the relationship between Washington and Jerusalem, the war with Iran and Israel’s domestic political divisions are emerging as key issues in the campaign.

description:
A devastating fire at a military training base in Wainwright, Alberta, has caused casualties and placed significant pressure on local medical services, with some injured people transferred to hospitals in other towns.

Local resident Brandon Simmons described a chaotic scene, comparing it to a war movie and recalling the sounds of people trapped in vehicles as the fire spread.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney addressed the nation, mourning those who lost their lives and saying they had been training to defend Canada. He described the incident as one of the country's worst peacetime tragedies for its armed forces.

Authorities are investigating the cause of the fast-moving blaze as the community and the country respond to the tragedy.

Al Jazeera’s Imogen Kimber reports.
